<h1>Md Bodrud-Doza, PhD</h1>
<p class="appointment">Environmental and geospatial scientist</p>
<p class="affiliation"><a href="https://geg.uoguelph.ca/">Department of Geography, Environment and Geomatics</a> · <a href="https://www.uoguelph.ca/">University of Guelph</a>, Ontario, Canada</p>
<p class="hero-intro">I work out where conservation actions can improve water quality while keeping agricultural land productive.</p>
<p>My research combines watershed modelling, geospatial analysis and machine learning with the priorities of the people who manage the land. It builds on a PhD in precision conservation for tile-drained watersheds and on earlier work in climate adaptation and science–policy practice.</p>

## Research program

One question runs through my work: how can agricultural landscapes stay productive while protecting water, soil and ecosystems? I am developing the answer as a research program, the [REAL Decision Lab](research.qmd), built on three connected pillars.

<div class="cards three pillars"><article class="research-card"><p class="status-label">Established foundation</p><h3>Precision conservation and agricultural watershed science</h3><p>Nutrient transport, tile drainage, conservation-practice evaluation and field-scale targeting, informed by local priorities.</p></article><article class="research-card"><p class="status-label">Established methods · emerging applications</p><h3>Environmental intelligence: GIS, Earth observation and GeoAI</h3><p>Spatial analysis and machine learning are established parts of my work. Satellite observation and GeoAI are directions I am building.</p></article><article class="research-card"><p class="status-label">Developing direction</p><h3>Resilient agricultural landscapes and adaptive decision support</h3><p>Multi-benefit conservation, climate adaptation and decision tools that are updated as monitoring shows what worked.</p></article></div>

<p class="section-link"><a href="research.qmd#research-pillars">How the pillars connect, and the five-year plan →</a></p>
